words.form: drepr faður sín eða moðor dottor eða systur

cognate: Ved. mātṛ-hán-/pitṛ-hán- (AVP: mātṛhā pitṛhā svasṛhā) ~ Gk πατρο-φονεύς/μητρο-φόντης and φονεύς τῆς μητρός: kin term + agent of *gʷʰen- 'slay'
drift_or_renewal: ON renews the verb (drepa for *gʷʰen-) and uses a clause (drepr faður sinn eða móður ... systur), keeping the inherited kin terms in the same order type
shared_syntax: kin term as object/first member + agent noun of *gʷʰen- (Ved., Gk); kin term objects of 'kill' in a catalogue (ON)
context: Catalogue of the gravest offenders: AVP lists mother-, father-, sister-slayers among evil-doers whose stain is wiped off; Gk legal/tragic category of the father-/mother-slayer (Plato Laws lists πατροφόνον ἢ μητροκτόνον for the harshest penalty; Homer's πατροφονεύς Aegisthus); ON law (Magnús lagabœtir's landslǫg, AM 302 fol) lists killing father, mother, daughter, sister among the unatonable crimes. The Gk–Ved. compound with the same root is the core; the ON passage is a congruent legal catalogue with the verb renewed.
phrase: *méh2tr-/*ph2tr- gʷʰen- 'mother-/father-slayer' as category of the worst kin-crime
note: Both -han and -φόντης are productive compound types (vṛtrahán, Ἀργεϊφόντης), so independent formation is possible; kin-killing as worst crime is near-universal. ON is a late legal text; its link is only typological + kin cognates.

words: ann henni sem augum í hǫfði sér

search_lead.cognate: ON auga ~ Lat. oculus (*h3ekʷ- 'eye'); verb renewed (unna vs amare)
search_lead.argument: 'Love someone as (more than) one's own eyes' in ON saga (Njáls saga, here a daughter loved by her father) and Catullus (dear as/more than one's eyes, of a beloved): eye as the measure of dearness with the eye word cognate. Weak: a natural comparison, the verb is not cognate, Catullus may echo Greek/Hellenistic usage, and ON may owe something to biblical 'apple of the eye' (Deut 32:10, Ps 17:8).

near_miss.lead: ON þagði ... engi maðr fekk orð af honom ~ Lat. uerbum muttit ... tacet: þegja ~ taceo, orð ~ uerbum (both exact cognates)
near_miss.why_not: Both lexemes are exact cognates but the pairing 'silent, not a word' is semantically natural; collocates --pair gives 8/182 Germanic units (þegja ok mælti ekki orð is everyday saga prose) vs 1/94 Italic (only this Plautus line, where a door is the subject). No congruent context or figure.

near_miss.lead: ON legal 'líf eða limir' (life or limbs)
near_miss.why_not: Alliterative Germanic legal pair; no partner in the bundle continues it (Sanskrit partners share only 'be'/'see').

near_miss.lead: eye kennings (sól, ljós) ~ Arm. 'eye/source of light'
near_miss.why_not: Snorri's learned kenning list; Armenian is Christian Psalm-based light imagery; no shared collocation.
Different lexemes (orð vs rota); generic treaty language.

near_miss.lead: truth vs lie: ON sannr/ljúga ~ ORu право/лжа
near_miss.why_not: ljúga ~ lъža cognate but the truth word is renewed and the true/false antithesis is generic.

near_miss.lead: ON um várit ... vinna ~ Lat. it uer et Venus
near_miss.why_not: vinna 'work/take land' and Venus share a root only by mapping; no shared sense or figure; 'in spring' generic.

near_miss.lead: name with mother and father as identity (Ir. na fes ainm na máthair na athair; Od. 9.366-7 name given by μήτηρ ἠδὲ πατήρ; ON gaf nafn sitt with móðurfaðir)
near_miss.why_not: Kin terms and 'name' co-occur everywhere; asking name and parentage is universal; ON is name-giving by a maternal grandfather, a different situation.
Verb+object is semantically trivial; ON is the pagan water-sprinkling naming rite, Od. is fetching water: no congruent context; cognacy of ἀφύσσω with ausa is itself doubtful.

near_miss.lead: ON í blóma aldrs / nýr ~ Lat. nouos ... flores
near_miss.why_not: Different figures (bloom of age vs picking new flowers); new/flower co-occurrence generic.

near_miss.lead: genealogical 'took a wife, daughter of X'; AVŚ duhitā iva pitaram svam
near_miss.why_not: Genealogical kin-term prose is generic; no shared syntagm beyond kin nouns.

near_miss.lead: tongue and heart pair (ON tunga ... samþykk hjarta ~ AVŚ hṛdayaṃ ... jihvāṃ)
near_miss.why_not: ON is the Third Grammatical Treatise translating a Latin rhetorical definition; AVŚ is a curse on body parts; heart+tongue pairing generic.
Poet-as-craftsman metaphor is of interest but no partner in the bundle has it (Greek partners are prose about battle order).
